ai.title: Add CSS test case to generatePatch suite
ai.summary: Added test fixture for CSS file patching. Includes `old.ts`, `new.ts`, and `expected.ts` mock data. Registered in `generate-patch.test.ts` via `runPatchTest` on `src/style.css`. Internal QA only.

eli5.text: Nothing for you to see here. The team added a new test case that checks whether their patching tool handles CSS files correctly, using three sample files that represent what the tool should do. It’ all internal: this test runs automatically when they run their checks, and if it passes, the tool is confirmed to work on CSS without breaking anything. You won’t notice any difference in your project unless a future change breaks this test, which would alert the team before it reaches you.

ai.title: Cap web scraper output at 75k chars
ai.summary: Added MAX_SCRAPED_CONTENT_LENGTH constant (75,000 chars) to npm-app/src/web-scraper.ts. getScrapedContentBlocks now truncates scraped content exceeding this limit, appending '[...TRUNCATED: WEB PAGE CONTENT TOO LONG...]'. This prevents oversized web content from bloating prompt tokens. Scope limited to the web scraper module in the npm-app package.

eli5.text: When you ask the assistant to pull in information from a web page, it now stops reading once it has gathered about 75,000 characters, roughly a 150-page novel, and adds a small note saying the rest was cut off. This applies only to the internal web-fetching tool, so any page you scrape that runs longer than that limit will come back shortened instead of filling up the request you send to the assistant. The change went live today and affects anyone whose workflow depends on that scraper, meaning very large pages may now return less detail than they did before.

ai.title: Pricing page adds Discord link to Community support
ai.summary: The Free tier's 'Community support' feature on the pricing page is now a clickable link to the Discord server (https://discord.gg/mcWTGjgTj3). This change affects web/src/app/pricing/page.tsx, replacing plain text with a Link component.

eli5.text: On the pricing page, the words 'Community support' under the Free plan are now a clickable link that takes you straight to the project's Discord server (https://discord.gg/mcWTGjgTj3). If you visit the pricing page and look at what the Free plan offers, you'll see 'Community support' as a link you can click, instead of plain text. Now if you're on the Free tier and need help from the community, you can click through to join the discussion on Discord directly. This change applies to everyone viewing the pricing page.

ai.title: Pro overage cost raised to $0.90 per 100 credits
ai.summary: Pro tier overage allowance updated from $0.50 to $0.90 per 100 credits in `web/src/app/pricing/page.tsx`. Documentation in `web/knowledge.md` expanded to explicitly define the new pricing structure. Support description refined to 'Priority support over email'.

ai.title: Pricing page copy and layout fixes
ai.summary: Updated `web/src/app/pricing/page.tsx` to simplify overage copy, add credit context, and fix card layout. Changed Pro plan text to '$0.90 per 100 credits afterwards' and added a note that '500 credits is equivalent to a multi-hour work session'. Applied flexbox to pricing cards for consistent height and set `target="_blank"` on community support links.

eli5.text: The pricing page now explains what you get more clearly: it tells you that 1,000 credits cost $0.99 to add once you've used your monthly allotment, and that 500 credits is roughly enough to run the assistant for a few hours. The three plan boxes are also now the same height, and clicking the link to the community support Discord will open it in a new browser tab instead of taking you away from the page. These updates appear when you visit the pricing page today.

ai.title: Referral page prompt copy updated
ai.summary: `web/src/app/referrals/page.tsx` updated the non-limit referral prompt. The copy now reads `Refer a friend and earn ${CREDITS_REFERRAL_BONUS} credits per month! Share this link with them:` instead of the generic send-link message. Scope is limited to the Web referrals page. The change uses `CREDITS_REFERRAL_BONUS` interpolation in user-facing copy.

eli5.text: You now see a clearer message on the referrals page: instead of the generic 'Send this link to your friend,' you're told you'll earn a set number of monthly credits for each friend you refer. The wording specifically mentions the credits you get per referral. The change is live today on the Web referrals page.
